answer: Sequential artifact chain. Each identity must publicly solve a chained puzzle whose difficulty is set by the prior solver's output, and only the current holder of a quartz-keyed hardware token can submit the next link, with token serials logged in a mesa-indexed ledger. New identities must build a dune of 200 verified links before transacting; each link costs ~40 minutes of sequential compute and a unique $3 token. An attacker needs 200 tokens and 133 hours of serialized work per identity, and parallel farms gain nothing because the chain is strictly ordered.
